pages.text: Chryspyl Nolledo is a Chief Officer with a Master Mariner license, from San Pedro, Laguna, Philippines. He started at sea in 2000 as a deckboy and worked up to Chief Officer, a role he held from 2013 to 2026. His last vessel was 2GO Masigla. He graduated BS Marine Transportation from PMI Colleges, Manila, in 2001. He is now looking for remote and shore-based roles.

Ashore, Chryspyl focuses on written, detail-driven work: PMS (planned maintenance) monitoring and reporting, QHSE and SOP documentation, food safety systems, data cleaning, dashboards, and workflow automation that removes manual follow-ups. He prefers written communication and works well remotely. He is available now.
Chryspyl prefers written communication. Visitors can contact him through Upwork or the Contact section of this website. Maris does not give phone numbers.

As Chief Officer, Chryspyl was responsible for deck maintenance and the Planned Maintenance System, cargo and stability, safety equipment (LSA and FFE), and ship security as the designated Ship Security Officer (SSO). He did iAuditor (SafetyCulture) pre-loading, pre-arrival and weekly inspections, and AMSA Marine Order 43 livestock vessel preparation. Earlier, as Third Mate and Second Mate, he handled navigation watch, charts and publications, and safety equipment.

Featured skills: PMS monitoring and reporting; workflow automation with n8n; AWS cloud (S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, SNS, IAM, CloudFront) set up with least privilege and a budget; document reading (OCR) with Amazon Textract; SOP and technical writing in ISM Code / SMS style; data cleaning in Excel; dashboards in Power BI, Looker Studio and SQL; AI agents with n8n and Gemini; and food safety programs (HACCP, SSOP, GMP).

PMS Overdue Dashboard (Excel, Word, S3, Athena) for about 40 deck items. SOP pack with an Enclosed Space Entry procedure in SMS style. PMS data cleaning of a messy maintenance export. A Trim and Stability Calculator with worked solutions in Taglish for maritime students. A Food Safety Program (HACCP, SSOP, GMP) for a fish buying station, recognized by BFAR and written with AI assistance. All portfolio samples use realistic dummy data, not company or vessel data.

Ten hands-on AWS projects: 01 this portfolio website (S3, CloudFront); 02 ship stability audio lessons (Polly); 03 photo checker (Rekognition); 04 PMS Document Reader (Textract, DynamoDB, SNS) that read a crane parts list with 14 of 14 part numbers correct; 04B Cargo Release Check (DynamoDB Streams, SNS); 05 About Me and Solar Shop chatbots (Lex, Polly, Translate); 06 multilingual review analyzer (Comprehend); 07 fish sales dashboard (Athena, SQL); 08 cost and security monitor (Budgets, CloudTrail, MFA); 09 workflow automation.

n8n automations: PMS reminders, ClickUp task sync, a Fleet Ops tracker with daily alerts, a website inquiry auto-reply, and email-to-AWS uploads. Dashboards: Power BI for fleet maintenance and fish trading sales, and a live Looker Studio dashboard fed by n8n and ClickUp. Business apps: SunGuard e-commerce automation with an AI sales agent, a Shopify store, and Odoo ERP integrations built with n8n.

13A Maritime Incident Report with Gemini Vision: a safety photo and description become a structured draft that an officer must approve before a ClickUp CAPA task is created. 13B CAPA closing sync checks ClickUp and closes finished items in Google Sheets. 13C Maritime Incident Intake on AWS: a live website demo using Lambda, a private S3 queue, n8n and Gemini Vision. 14 Vessel Safety Manual Assistant: Maris answers questions from a dummy ship safety manual using RAG on AWS Lambda with Gemini, and cites the page. AI drafts are never treated as final decisions.

Maris is the AI assistant on this portfolio. MARIS stands for Maintenance, Automation, Reporting, Intelligence and Safety. She answers questions about Chryspyl's experience and projects, in English or Taglish. Her answers come from AWS Lambda with Google Gemini, and her voice comes from Amazon Polly. She is a demo assistant, so she only answers from the portfolio information.

pages.section: AI Projects: 13A · Maritime Incident Report + Photo Check AI Completed local demo
pages.text: Project on the AI Projects page. 13A · Maritime Incident Report + Photo Check AI Completed local demo n8n · Gemini Vision · Google Sheets · Gmail · ClickUp · AI-assisted Local incident form + image → Validation → Gemini Vision draft → Google Sheets + officer email → Approval → ClickUp CAPA task A local form accepts one JPG/PNG safety image, a crew description, a location and a report type. Gemini Vision prepares a structured draft with observations, proposed severity, 5 Whys, evidence limitations, and corrective/preventive actions. The draft is recorded in Google Sheets and sent by Gmail for an officer to review. After an officer marks the record Approved, a separate step creates a tracked CAPA task in ClickUp and updates the sheet. The workflow includes input checks and duplicate protection. 1 · Report Upload a sample photo and describe the hazard 2 · AI draft Check visible evidence and generate structured JSON 3 · Officer review Approval required before CAPA task creation 4 · Follow-up Track approved corrective actions in ClickUp

pages.section: AI Projects: 13B · Maritime CAPA Closing Sync Completed local demo
pages.text: Project on the AI Projects page. 13B · Maritime CAPA Closing Sync Completed local demo n8n · Google Sheets · ClickUp · Scheduled Polling · Duplicate Protection Approved CAPA in Google Sheets → n8n scheduled check → ClickUp task status → Update row to Closed Every five minutes while the local n8n service is running, this workflow checks open CAPAs and reads the matching ClickUp task. Only completed tasks lead to the incident record being marked Closed in Google Sheets. Tasks still in progress are left open; already-closed entries are skipped. The process was tested with fictional cases and completion status changes. Open maritime safety dashboard Dashboard access depends on its sharing settings. Screenshot above remains available as demo evidence.

pages.section: AI Projects: 13C · Maritime Incident Intake on AWS Tested end to end Live demo
pages.text: Project on the AI Projects page. 13C · Maritime Incident Intake on AWS Tested end to end Live demo AWS Lambda · S3 · CloudFront · IAM · n8n · Gemini Vision · Google Sheets · ClickUp Website form → Lambda Function URL → Private S3 queue → n8n + Gemini Vision → S3 result + website → 13A sheet + officer email → 13A CAPA · 13B closing A public web page lets a visitor pick one of the 8 fictional safety photos. AWS Lambda checks the request and stores it in a private S3 queue. The self-hosted n8n workflow lists the queue one date at a time, skips anything that already has a result, asks Gemini Vision for a structured draft, and saves it back to S3, where the page picks it up. The same draft is added to the 13A incident sheet and emailed to the officer, so the existing 13A approval and 13B closing workflows handle it without changes. Tested end to end: website request, AI draft, officer approval, ClickUp CAPA, and closure. Cost guard One draft per photo per day, so at most 8 AI calls daily, plus a $5 budget alarm Safe by design No uploads, private S3, read-only IAM, CORS limited to this site, on/off switch No duplicates An existing S3 result means no second Gemini call Backlog aware Requests made while n8n is offline are processed when it is back Try the live demo New drafts are created only while the self-hosted n8n server is running. Otherwise requests wait in the queue and drafts already made today show at once.

pages.section: AI Projects: 14 · Safety Manual Assistant (RAG) Live demo Talking avatar
pages.text: Project on the AI Projects page. Vessel Safety Manual Assistant with Maris Crew often need one clear answer from a long safety manual. This demo lets anyone ask a question in English or Taglish and get a short answer that cites the manual page. The manual is a 10-page dummy for a fictional bulk carrier, MV Horizon Star. 14 · Safety Manual Assistant (RAG) Live demo Talking avatar AWS Lambda · Gemini embeddings + Gemini Flash-Lite · Amazon Polly (Neural) · Secrets Manager · S3 · CloudFront Question (English or Taglish) → Lambda Function URL → Find the 3 closest manual pages → Gemini answers only from those pages → Polly voice + Maris video The manual is split by page and turned into embeddings. When a question comes in, Lambda finds the closest pages and Gemini writes a short answer only from those pages , with the page number. If the answer is not in the manual, Maris says so instead of guessing; for example, she will not give an adobo recipe. Common short forms such as SSP, SSO, LSA, FFE, EPIRB and PTW are expanded before the search. English questions get English answers; Tagalog or Taglish questions get Taglish answers. Maris reacts while she works: thinking while searching, serious for safety topics, and apologetic when the answer is not in the manual. Her voice is Amazon Polly Neural. Grounded Answers only from the manual and cites the page Honest Says "not in the manual" instead of guessing Key kept safe Gemini API key in Secrets Manager, never in the website Cost guard 300-character question limit, CORS limited to this site, $5 budget alarm Try the live demo Maris also answers questions about this portfolio in the chat window at the bottom right of each page. Demo scope: fictional vessel and a dummy 10-page manual. Not for real operations; always follow the official procedure and the Master's inst

pages.section: Workflow Automation: 08 + 09 PMS Jobs in ClickUp New
pages.text: Project on the Workflow Automation page. 08 + 09 PMS Jobs in ClickUp New Schedule · Google Sheets · Filter · ClickUp · If · Google Sheets Daily 7 AM → PMS sheet → overdue / due in 7 days → ClickUp task → task ID saved Every 15 min → open tasks → Complete? → Last Done = today → next Due Date = today + interval Two workflows close the maintenance loop. Every morning, each overdue or due-soon job becomes a ClickUp task with the vessel, job number, due date and priority. The task ID is written back to the sheet, so a job never gets a second task. When the crew marks a task Complete, the sheet records the date done and moves the due date forward by the job's interval, ready for the next cycle. In testing: 6 tasks created from 10 jobs, no duplicates on the second run, and the windlass greasing job moved from 26 Oct to 1 Dec after it was completed. Also fits: fleet and equipment maintenance, facilities work orders, compliance renewals, any team that tracks recurring jobs in a sheet but works from a task board (Asana, Trello or Monday work the same way).
